step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified core infrastructure components from the visual diagram and audio transcript: CloudFront, AWS Shield, ECS, Kinesis Firehose, S3, Lambda, DynamoDB, and API Gateway.
2. Pruned generic stick figures (actors) per Rule 5, using system entry/exit points (CloudFront, API Gateway) for workflow routing.
3. Mapped all service names directly to valid AWS vocabulary types.
4. Structured distinct logical flows:
   - Flow 0: Raw ad interaction ingestion via CloudFront -> ECS -> Kinesis Firehose -> S3 raw storage.
   - Flow 1: Periodic batch aggregation by Lambda pulling from S3 and writing aggregated outputs to S3 and DynamoDB.
   - Flow 2: Analytics dashboard querying from API Gateway to DynamoDB and S3, with routing to CloudFront.
   - Flow 3: AWS Shield protection covering traffic to prevent cost scaling during DDoS attacks.

graph.name: Equinix Serverless Ad Tech Ingestion and Analytics Architecture
graph.notes: Serverless ad tech platform handling up to 15,000 events per second. Uses CloudFront, ECS container receivers in Go, Kinesis Firehose, S3, Lambda, DynamoDB, API Gateway, and AWS Shield for DDoS/cost protection.

nodes.name: CloudFront
nodes.notes: Receives user web interaction events (clicks, impressions).

nodes.name: Shield
nodes.notes: Provides DDoS and cost protection against attack traffic spikes.

nodes.name: ECS
nodes.notes: Docker cluster running Go receiver services.

nodes.name: Kinesis Firehose
nodes.notes: Aggregates and streams raw events to storage.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Stores raw user interaction data and processed analytical datasets.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Stores aggregated metrics and key business outputs.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Fronts backend requests for real-time analytics data.

edges.notes: CloudFront routes incoming user ad interaction events to ECS receivers.
ECS Go receivers push event messages to Kinesis Firehose.
Kinesis Firehose writes raw streaming interaction logs into S3.
Lambda reads raw event data from S3 every 5 minutes.
Lambda writes aggregated output analytics back into S3.
Lambda populates aggregated query results into DynamoDB tables.
API Gateway retrieves aggregated analytics metrics from DynamoDB.
API Gateway queries analytical data stored in S3.
API Gateway connects back across CloudFront distribution network.
CloudFront edge traffic is monitored and protected by AWS Shield.
Shield mitigates attack volume to safeguard backend storage cost models.
